what: FMT/rCDI mechanism-decomposition: 7 ablation arms on a 5-member gapseq community (4 donors + C. difficile 630), raw yields (no dials), western_gut ModelSEED medium, 120h dFBA. Ran in parallel on ts-02.
metric_note: rebound_lambda (>0 = pathogen regrowing) is the durability metric; the 'cleared' flag is the vegetative-min snapshot and reads dormancy as cure -- misleading.
verdict_qualitative: CLEAN ablation recovers Buffie 2015: removing pH changes nothing (lambda 0.0087->0.0087, INERT); removing bile raises lambda (0.0087->0.0119, ~28% faster rebound) -> SECONDARY BILE ACIDS are the sole load-bearing arm; nutrient competition alone (fmt_competition == fmt_no_bile) does nothing here. From genomes + stoichiometry, no fitted yields.
honest_limitation: NO arm achieves durable clearance (lambda>0 everywhere -> C.diff always rebounds; bile only SLOWS it). Root cause: C. scindens grows 0.0008/h on this medium -> under-establishes -> under-produces deoxycholate -> bile arm under-powered. SAME reconstruction/yield bottleneck as the Clark under-growers.
throughline: muODE gets the MECHANISM right in both acts (competition ranking in Clark, bile effector in FMT) but the QUANTITATIVE strength in both is limited by reconstruction/yield quality. Clark fixed it via OD calibration; C.scindens has no such correction. The yield/reconstruction lever is the UNIFYING problem.
